newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money slumps at month-end.
newsitem.headline: German call money slumps at month-end.

text.p: German call money became clearly cheaper at month-end on Friday, trading near 2.50 percent, and traders said liquidity conditions were so ample that rates could even slump towards the 1.50 percent level.
The session began with funds trading just under the three percent level that has been seen in recent sessions. By mid-session rates had dipped to 2.50 percent, dealers said.
"The mass of liquidity could mean that rates could even dip as low as 1.5 percent," one dealer said, joking funds were so cheap, its was becoming difficult to give the money away.

One key for the dramatic liquidity overhang is that banks have more than met their monthly reserve requirements, holding 44.6 billion marks at the Bundesbank on Wednesday, far above the expected goal of around 40 billion marks. The monthly average on Wednesday was unchanged at 41.1 billion marks.

"The Bundesbank had pumped so much liquidity into the market that by now even the thickest trader should have realised that he does not need to borrow at the Lombard, emergency rate," another trader said.
Separately traders said another reason for easier rates might be renewed hope the Bundesbank is preparing a rate cut.

After nearly one year of watching the Bundesbank keep its main money market rate, the repo, fixed at three percent, dealers said that there may be a chance the repo could be cut to 2.75 percent in line with preparations for currency union.
The repo has been fixed at three percent since August.

"There is a chance that the future European central bank will not have a discount rate (historically the floor for German interest rates). In order to prepare for that, the Bundesbank might consider lowering its repo rate again, possibly to 2.75 percent some time in the longer term," a trader said.
Dealers agreed that such speculation could be seen putting any fears of a near-term rate hike on ice.
But next week, dealers expect the new month will be started with money market rates around three percent again, as month-end gyrations in rates ofen work themselves out early in the next month.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average was set at 2.64000 percent on Friday compared with 2.69733 percent.
